title: Customer Reviews as Growth Tool for Sellers
description: Amazon published a guide teaching sellers how to leverage customer reviews as market research and convert ratings into business growth opportunities. This content targets active sellers looking to optimize their performance on the platform. It serves as an engagement and retention mechanism by providing actionable value to existing sellers.

title: Guided Experience for Reporting Brand Violations Faster
description: Amazon announced a new streamlined, guided experience for reporting brand violations, reducing friction in the brand protection process. This signals an investment in seller trust and brand registry tooling. It primarily benefits brand-registered sellers who need efficient IP and listing protection workflows.

title: Margin Calculation Guide for E-commerce Products
description: Amazon published an educational article on how to calculate margins for e-commerce products using Amazon tools. This onboarding-oriented content helps prospects and new sellers understand unit economics before or after listing. It lowers the barrier to entry by demystifying profitability calculations.

title: FBA Fee Education to Help Sellers Maximize Profit
description: Amazon released a beginner-focused article explaining how FBA fees work and how sellers can structure their business to maximize profit. This content addresses a common friction point that causes seller hesitation or churn around fulfillment costs. It supports both new seller conversion and retention by increasing fee transparency.

title: Inventory Management Guide for Small Businesses
description: Amazon published a 7-minute read on inventory management tailored for small business sellers. This educational content helps sellers avoid stockouts and overstock issues, directly impacting listing health and sales performance. It serves as a retention lever by building seller competency and reducing avoidable listing suppression.

title: Seller Café Personalized Support at Amazon Accelerate 2026
description: Amazon announced a 'Seller Café' experience at Amazon Accelerate 2026 offering personalized, one-on-one support sessions for sellers. This in-person touchpoint is a high-engagement retention tactic designed to deepen seller relationships and resolve platform pain points. It targets active sellers seeking direct access to Amazon support and product teams.

title: International Expansion Guide with 5 Actionable Tips
description: Amazon published a detailed 11-minute guide on expanding seller businesses to international marketplaces. This growth-oriented content is aimed at established domestic sellers ready to scale cross-border. It acts as a retention and upsell lever by encouraging sellers to deepen their commitment to the Amazon ecosystem globally.

title: FBA Prep, Packaging, and Labeling Beginner's Guide
description: Amazon released a beginner's guide covering FBA prep, packaging, and labeling requirements. This onboarding content reduces new seller errors that commonly lead to shipment rejections and early churn. It directly supports the listing and fulfillment activation stage for sellers transitioning to FBA.

title: Seller University Now Available to Everyone
description: Amazon announced that Seller University, its educational training platform, is now publicly accessible to all users, not just registered sellers. This significantly lowers the barrier to entry for prospects considering selling on Amazon. It is a direct acquisition lever that nurtures potential sellers through education before they commit to registration.

title: Over $50,000 in New Seller Incentives Promotion
description: Amazon is prominently promoting a new seller incentives package worth over $50,000 to attract prospective sellers to the platform. This financial incentive bundle is a top-of-funnel acquisition tool designed to convert prospects by reducing perceived financial risk. It likely includes credits for FBA, advertising, and other platform services to accelerate early seller activation.

title: Depop publishes 'How to grow your shop' seller guide
description: Depop published a dedicated 'How to grow your shop' article on April 1, 2026 via their blog hub, The Depop Circular. This type of educational content targets sellers looking to scale their activity on the platform. It signals an investment in seller success content as a retention and engagement lever.

title: Monthly 'Trending on Depop' series drives listing relevance signals
description: Depop publishes a recurring monthly 'Trending on Depop' series covering categories like vintage jerseys, tennis wear, and seasonal styles. This content serves as implicit merchandising guidance, nudging sellers to list trending items to improve their sales potential. It acts as a soft listing tool and search visibility aid for active sellers.

title: The Depop Circular blog hub centralizes seller and community engagement
description: Depop has established The Depop Circular as a centralized content hub covering product features, community updates, and trend inspiration. This hub functions as an always-on engagement channel to keep sellers informed and connected to the platform ecosystem. It supports both new seller onboarding and ongoing retention by maintaining platform stickiness.

title: Sunset current consignment program; launch purpose-built 'consignment as a service'
description: Poshmark is retiring its existing consignment model and transitioning to a specialized 'consignment as a service' offering with physical infrastructure for expert authentication, white-glove intake, and dedicated fulfillment. The new model is designed to unlock high-value luxury inventory from sellers whose items would otherwise sit idle. Gradual access rollout will be tied to available facility capacity.

title: Acquire Linda's Stuff operational facilities to power luxury consignment infrastructure
description: Poshmark has acquired the dedicated operational facilities of Linda's Stuff to support its next-generation consignment service. These facilities will be repurposed exclusively for Poshmark sellers as Linda's Stuff legacy inventory is wound down. The infrastructure investment is aimed at attracting qualified luxury buyers and driving incremental traffic and sales across the broader marketplace.

title: Remove Excessive Listing Removal policy to ease seller inventory management
description: Poshmark is eliminating its Excessive Listing Removal policy, which previously penalized sellers for keeping unavailable or duplicate listings live. Sellers will now be free to delete listings at will and manage their closets according to their own business needs without compliance risk. This change directly responds to seller community feedback about the policy's burden on day-to-day operations.

title: Publish actionable listing optimization tips tied to impression and click funnel
description: Poshmark shared a structured funnel-based framework helping sellers diagnose and fix listing performance issues—covering low impressions, high impressions with low clicks, and clicks without offers. Recommendations include refreshing titles/descriptions, adjusting prices, improving cover photos, and updating sizing details. This guidance is designed to drive conversion improvements from existing inventory without requiring new listings.

title: Promote Smart Sell automation with '60% more likely to sell in 7 days' claim
description: Poshmark is actively promoting its Smart Sell feature as an automated negotiation tool, citing a 60% higher likelihood of a sale within the first 7 days for enrolled listings. The feature is positioned as a key lever for sellers looking to increase sales velocity with minimal manual effort. This nudge is embedded in seller communications to drive adoption among sellers who have not yet enabled the feature.

title: Launch new Seller Hub as centralized business management dashboard
description: Poshmark is introducing a redesigned Seller Hub described as the biggest change yet to closet management, consolidating key actions, alerts, and growth tools in a single streamlined interface. The hub is intended to surface a seller's next best action and reduce the operational overhead of running a closet. The redesign signals a significant UX investment to improve daily engagement and reduce seller churn.

title: Overhaul Smart List AI to enable snap-and-list in seconds via photo
description: Poshmark is fully overhauling its Smart List AI feature to allow sellers to create complete, priced, and described listings simply by taking a photo with their phone. The goal is to reduce listing friction to near zero, making it as easy as snapping a picture. A beta testing cohort is being recruited via a sign-up link embedded in the seller update.

title: Launch performance-based seller recognition program with search visibility rewards
description: Poshmark is rolling out a new tiered seller program launching in October that grants qualifying sellers elevated search visibility and a buyer-facing trust signal. Qualification requires 20 lifetime orders plus rolling 90-day metrics: 5+ orders or $500 in sales, ≤2-day average ship time, and ≤2% cancellation and return rates. Buyers will be able to filter search results to surface only these high-performing sellers, creating a strong retention and performance incentive.

title: Introduce Posh Stats within Seller Tools for performance self-assessment
description: Poshmark is surfacing a new Posh Stats section inside Seller Tools to let sellers check their standing against the new performance program criteria in real time. This gives sellers a data-driven feedback loop to understand where they fall short before the October program launch. The tool is designed to drive behavioral change toward faster shipping, lower cancellations, and higher fulfillment rates.

title: Test streamlined pre-search UX that repositions People search in autocomplete
description: Poshmark is A/B testing a revised pre-search experience that moves People search from a dedicated tab to the bottom of autocomplete suggestions, temporarily removing the Posh Ambassador section from the pre-search page. The change aims to streamline the search entry point and may affect seller discoverability through profile-based search. This test could impact traffic flows to individual seller closets depending on results.

title: Absorb 100% of USPS HAZMAT non-compliance fees through July 31, then share cost 90/10
description: In response to a new USPS $50 Hazardous Materials non-compliance fee effective July 12, 2026, Poshmark is absorbing the full fee for sellers through July 31 and covering 90% ($45) from August 1 onward. This temporary subsidy protects sellers from an unexpected cost during a policy transition period. The tiered coverage structure acts as a seller protection measure while shifting partial compliance responsibility to sellers over time.

title: Publish HAZMAT shipping compliance education guide for sellers
description: Poshmark is proactively distributing step-by-step guidance to help sellers avoid USPS HAZMAT fees, focusing on inspection of reused boxes, removal of old hazmat labels, and electronics-specific lithium-ion battery packaging requirements. The educational content reduces seller risk of accidental fees and supports shipping compliance at scale. A support escalation path is also provided for sellers who believe they were charged in error.

title: eBay launches AI photo-to-listing tool for sellers
description: eBay rolled out a tool that automatically generates product listings from photos, reducing friction in the listing creation process. This directly addresses one of the most common drop-off points in the seller journey by automating tedious data entry. It lowers the barrier for new and occasional sellers to get items live quickly.

title: Influur marketplace differentiates by promising timely payouts to influencers
description: Influur, an influencer marketplace, is using guaranteed timely payouts as a key retention and acquisition differentiator against competitors. Reliable payment flows directly address a major pain point for marketplace sellers and service providers, improving trust and reducing churn. This signals that payout reliability is becoming a competitive lever in marketplace seller retention.

title: DoorDash partners with Meta to enable delivery for Facebook Marketplace items
description: DoorDash tested a partnership with Meta to offer delivery fulfillment for items listed on Facebook Marketplace, creating a new fulfillment entry point for peer-to-peer sellers. This integration lowers the logistics barrier for casual and occasional sellers who lack shipping infrastructure. It signals a trend of embedding fulfillment solutions directly into listing platforms to increase conversion.

title: Temu faces stricter EU rules as a 'very large online platform'
description: The EU designated Temu as a 'very large online platform' under the Digital Services Act, subjecting it to stricter compliance and transparency requirements. This regulatory pressure could affect how Temu onboards and manages third-party sellers operating within the EU. Competing marketplaces may use this as an opportunity to attract sellers seeking a more compliant and stable environment.

title: NFT marketplace raises $2.5M to retain users during low-revenue periods
description: Former web3 gaming founders raised $2.5M to build an NFT marketplace explicitly focused on retaining users even when there 'isn't money to be made,' signaling investment in non-monetary engagement hooks. This approach highlights a structural challenge in marketplace retention: keeping sellers and buyers engaged during market downturns. It suggests engagement-first retention mechanics are becoming a funded strategy in marketplace design.

title: Promoted raises funding to help e-commerce marketplaces achieve profitability
description: Promoted secured additional funding to provide sponsored listing and search ranking tools to e-commerce marketplaces, helping them monetize traffic while improving seller visibility. This signals growing demand for on-platform advertising products as a dual lever for marketplace revenue and seller acquisition of buyers. It reinforces search visibility and fees/monetization as tightly linked levers in marketplace strategy.

title: Groupon cuts 500+ staff and pivots to mission-critical activities only
description: Groupon announced layoffs of over 500 employees and a strategic pivot to focus only on core operations, signaling significant contraction of its marketplace operations. This could represent a major disruption to merchant and seller relationships built on the platform. Competing marketplaces may see an opportunity to acquire displaced Groupon sellers and merchants through targeted reactivation campaigns.

title: Fleek raises $20.4M for wholesale secondhand clothes marketplace
description: Fleek secured $20.4M to scale its B2B wholesale marketplace for secondhand clothing, targeting resellers and vintage buyers as its primary seller segment. The funding signals strong investor appetite for resale-focused marketplace models with structured wholesale supply chains. This creates a new resell entry point for sellers transitioning from consumer resale to wholesale operations.

title: Pickle peer-to-peer fashion rental marketplace raises $8M
description: Pickle, a peer-to-peer fashion rental platform, raised $8M to expand its marketplace where individuals can rent out their clothing. This model activates a new seller segment — everyday consumers with wardrobes — as rental income earners on a marketplace platform. Onboarding flows for this segment must balance simplicity with trust-building around item condition and returns.

title: Wikifarmer leverages agricultural knowledge base to drive marketplace participation
description: Wikifarmer uses its agricultural knowledge content platform as a funnel to attract farmers into its marketplace, blending education with commerce. This content-to-commerce strategy serves as an acquisition and onboarding tool for a non-traditional seller segment. It highlights how value-added content can reduce acquisition costs and build seller trust before a transaction occurs.
